description: Strategy design module (entries, exits, position sizing, risk controls) for validated hypotheses, and the main pipeline orchestrator that runs the complete research process end-to-end with comprehensive reporting.
steps: Create src/quant_research/strategy/entries_exits.py - EntryExitDesigner class: for each validated hypothesis, designs entry rules (signal threshold, confirmation requirements, filter conditions), designs exit rules (time-based exit, signal reversal, trailing stop, profit target, stop-loss), supports multiple exit types: fixed stop/target, ATR-based adaptive stops, trailing stops, time-decay exits, tests combinations of entry/exit rules on in-sample data, selects best entry/exit combination based on risk-adjusted returns not raw returns

Create src/quant_research/strategy/position_sizing.py - PositionSizer class: implements multiple position sizing methods: fixed fractional (Kelly criterion), volatility-targeted (scale position to target vol), equal risk contribution, maximum drawdown-constrained, computes optimal position size for each strategy, enforces maximum position limits and portfolio-level risk budgets

Create src/quant_research/strategy/risk_controls.py - RiskController class: implements portfolio-level risk controls: maximum portfolio heat (total risk budget), correlation-based position limits (reduce size when strategies are correlated), drawdown circuit breaker (reduce size after X% drawdown), regime-based scaling (reduce in high-vol regimes), daily/weekly loss limits, tracks strategy-level and portfolio-level metrics

Create src/quant_research/reporting/results.py - ResearchReporter class: generates comprehensive research report with: executive summary (how many hypotheses generated, tested, survived), detailed results for each surviving hypothesis (signal description, economic rationale, data limitations, in-sample stats, out-of-sample stats, regime analysis, net-of-cost performance), comparison table across all surviving strategies, data transparency section (explicitly noting what data was used and what limitations exist, especially re: order flow), visualizations: equity curves, drawdown charts, regime performance heatmap, hypothesis rejection funnel chart, saves report as markdown + CSV summary tables in results/ directory

Create src/quant_research/main.py - main pipeline orchestrator: fetches data via DataFetcher, computes features via FeatureEngine, generates hypotheses via HypothesisGenerator, runs initial statistical tests via StatisticalTester, applies rejection criteria via HypothesisRejector, validates survivors via ValidationPipeline (walk-forward + OOS + regime + costs), designs strategies for final survivors via EntryExitDesigner + PositionSizer + RiskController, generates final report via ResearchReporter, includes comprehensive logging throughout, handles errors gracefully with partial results reported, prints a data limitations disclaimer at the start acknowledging OHLCV-only constraints
Create tests/test_strategy.py - Test EntryExitDesigner produces valid entry/exit rules, test PositionSizer computes reasonable position sizes, test RiskController enforces limits correctly

Create tests/test_main.py - Integration test that runs the pipeline on a small synthetic dataset to verify all components connect correctly (mock yfinance, use 1 year of generated data with a known signal embedded)
Update README.md with project description, setup instructions, usage guide, architecture overview, and data limitations disclaimer
Run full test suite to verify everything passes
acceptance_criteria: EntryExitDesigner produces entry and exit rules for each validated hypothesis
PositionSizer implements at least Kelly criterion and volatility-targeting
ResearchReporter generates a markdown report with all specified sections
main.py orchestrates the full pipeline from data fetch to final report
README.md documents the project architecture, usage, and data limitations
Data limitations disclaimer is prominently displayed (noting OHLCV cannot provide true order flow)
pytest tests/ passes all tests including integration test
Pipeline handles edge cases (no surviving hypotheses, insufficient data) gracefully
